scope: Real isolated PostgreSQL failure/concurrency tests, paid-client API tests, bounded Claude calls on Hugo and Nuxt, then deterministic Open Graph regression cycles on Hugo, Gatsby and Nuxt.

fixed_defects.defect: A long PostgreSQL correction lease consumed an application-pool connection.
fixed_defects.before_fix: A one-connection application pool cannot run a normal SELECT while the lease is held.
fixed_defects.fix: A separate, bounded PostgreSQL correction pool holds session leases. Four concurrent payers can still read quotas through a one-connection application pool; a fifth lease is refused without waiting.
fixed_defects.limits: Four leases per worker, not a production capacity certification; worker count, database connection limits and session-compatible pooling still need deployment-specific sizing.

fixed_defects.defect: Terminating a PostgreSQL lease connection could still return apparent correction success.
fixed_defects.before_fix: The killed session loses its advisory lock but the unlock error is swallowed.
fixed_defects.fix: Verify session PID and advisory-lock ownership before GitHub writes, before quota charges and at successful operation exit. Lost, closed or invalidated leases fail with 503 and are never silently reacquired.
fixed_defects.limits: These checks do not make an already in-flight external GitHub request atomic with the database.

fixed_defects.defect: An unknown existing-PR state was treated as permission to generate another paid preview.
fixed_defects.before_fix: Network failure, empty/non-object responses and unknown states permit a new preview after an existing PR.
fixed_defects.fix: All four PR-producing correction gates use strict PR-state checks. Unknown state or tracking-store read failure returns 503 before another provider call, charge or GitHub write.
fixed_defects.limits: Missing or damaged PR metadata and task-write failures still require durable operation recovery.

fixed_defects.defect: Open Graph alignment remained blocked by the old crawl after a canonical HTTP-to-HTTPS repair.
fixed_defects.before_fix: The file already has a safe HTTPS canonical, but an og:url trailing-slash difference survives; real counters remain 4 to 1.
fixed_defects.fix: Prepare a deferred pair that activates only when the current file contains exactly the repaired HTTPS canonical. No insecure downgrade, speculative canonical or model fallback is allowed.
fixed_defects.after_fix: Real baseline/correction previews show 4 to 0 on Hugo, Gatsby and Nuxt, with no observed count increases or newly affected routes.

postgres_validation.isolation: Temporary local cluster, synthetic users/projects, no production database or system service used.
integration_coverage: Separate-process exclusion for the same payer and independent payers
Four simultaneous payers and bounded fifth-operation refusal
Repeated connection-pool checkout without leaked locks
postgres_validation.customer_api_note: Actual FastAPI/auth/CSRF/payer/quota behavior; GitHub and provider are deterministic stubs for financial and failure tests.

full_local_suite.skip_note: Nine opt-in PostgreSQL guard cases and two PostgreSQL customer cases; all eleven passed in the separate real PostgreSQL run.

verification.whitespace_note: Existing app.py trailing blanks were left untouched; no new whitespace issue was reported in db.py.

live_totals.cost_note: Sum of rounded per-call estimates in claude.log, not an invoice. Calls include target mapping and do not equal model-written file counts.

selected_results.note: Already repaired by the mechanical mixed-content pass, not by Claude.
Already repaired by the mechanical mixed-content pass, not by Claude.

historical_attribution_correction.old_interpretation: The surviving Open Graph mismatch was attributed to an insecure canonical outside the mechanical-only batch.
historical_attribution_correction.new_evidence: The mixed-content pass had already upgraded the canonical to HTTPS; the remaining mismatch was its trailing slash versus og:url. The old crawl prevented the OG rewriter from resuming after that upgrade.

evidence_limits: Real builds and before/after crawls prove only the observed fixture-preview scope, not every client or every occurrence.
Netlify previews inject noindex. A family absent from the unchanged baseline remains unverified, even with an after-counter of zero.
Canonical 4xx and internal HTTP links have separate positive-control HTML checks, not crawler-count certification.
Missing reciprocal hreflang remains unverified where indexability suppresses it; no patch is not a success.
Claude follow-up selected three family keys with at most four files per family. Two families actually needed model-written files; the HTTP canonical was already mechanically repaired.
Description variants and other AI-written families remain partial or unexercised.
remaining_release_checks: P0: Durable correction-operation journal and idempotent billing/recovery when GitHub accepts a write but quota/task persistence or the HTTP response fails; retry must not create duplicate paid work or conflicting PRs.
P1: Deployment-specific PostgreSQL worker/pool sizing, session-compatible pooling, process recycling and longer load tests.
P1: Remaining Claude-written families, complete description batches and indexability-sensitive hreflang positive controls.
P1: Real paid-account onboarding, GitHub permissions, quota renewal, upgrade/downgrade and Stripe/provider failures.
Review and deploy local changes, then supervised pilots using draft PRs and human review before broader automation.
